Congress has already allocated $12.5 billion to repair our nation's aging air traffic control system. Yet Secretary Duffy and the Trump Administration have only spent a fraction of this investment and are blaming a router instead of taking accountability for this monumental failure. We remember the more than 1,200 innocent people murdered by Hamas and Islamic Jihad. We remember every life stolen and every family shattered. We remember the victims of unimaginable brutality.

We mourn. We remember. And we recommit ourselves to building a future in which Israelis and Palestinians can live in security, freedom, and peace.

There must be a full and independent investigation into the alleged crimes and the role of the authorities who managed this case from the very beginning. Moreover, each and every one of us has a role in preventing violence against women by confronting wrongdoing and standing with survivors.

Our duty to serve the 9/11 community of victims and survivors extends far beyond the anniversary of September 11. Today I was honored to speak at the World Trade Center Environmental Health Center Symposium to support the clinical providers, researchers, and community advocates who care for victims of 9/11 health-related illnesses. 

I am proud to have passed the James Zadroga 9/11 Bill in 2010, which created the World Trade Center Health Program, and I urge fellow lawmakers to continue investing in the cutting-edge research around these 9/11 related diseases, spreading awareness of resources available to those who are still getting sick from these illnesses, and ensuring every victim can access the medical care they deserve.

Amtrak’s so-called “deal” to bring in the MTA was an unserious, extortionary attempt to further hand Penn Station over to Trump and Sean Duffy’s Department of Transportation.
